## Command

`ast-grep 0.51.1` at `/opt/homebrew/bin/ast-grep`. I used a rule file (kept outside the repo in `/tmp`, nothing in the repo was touched):

```bash
cat > /tmp/sg-probe/set-cookie.yml <<'YAML'
id: set-cookie-header
language: TypeScript
severity: info
message: Set-Cookie header string literal
rule:
  any:
    - kind: string
    - kind: template_string
  regex: (?i)set-cookie
YAML

ast-grep scan --rule /tmp/sg-probe/set-cookie.yml src adapters
```

Then a repo-wide confirmation run (same 95 hits, 18 files, nothing outside `src/` and `adapters/`):

```bash
ast-grep scan --rule /tmp/sg-probe/set-cookie.yml . 
```

Portable equivalent (verified, no temp file needed):

```bash
ast-grep scan --inline-rules 'id: set-cookie-header
language: TypeScript
severity: info
message: Set-Cookie header string literal
rule:
  any:
    - kind: string
    - kind: template_string
  regex: (?i)set-cookie' src adapters
```

Note: the rule matches *string nodes*, so comments/JSDoc are excluded — `src/helper/proxy/index.ts:134` (a doc comment saying `res.headers.delete('Set-Cookie')`) is correctly not a hit, though grep finds it.

---

## Runtime reads/writes (production source)

- `:422` read — `this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()` (implicit read of all Set-Cookie values)

- `:425` write — `_res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)` (per cookie, inside loop)
- `:619` read — `if (key === 'set-cookie')` when merging `arg.headers`
- `:620` write — `responseHeaders.append(key, value)` (append instead of set, i.e. the Set-Cookie write path)

`src/helper/cookie/index.ts` (the public writers)
- `:101` write — `c.header('Set-Cookie', cookie, { append: true })` in `setCookie`
- `:138` write — `c.header('set-cookie', cookie, { append: true })` in `setSignedCookie`

`src/middleware/cache/index.ts`
- `:80` read — `res.headers.has('Set-Cookie')` in `shouldSkipCache`

`src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts` (multi-value cookie extraction + response emission)
- `:187` read — `if (name === 'set-cookie')` in `res.headers.forEach` (pulls cookies out of headers)
- `:418` read — `res.headers.has('set-cookie')`
- `:419`–`420` read — `getSetCookie` feature test / call
- `:422` read — `.filter(([k]) => k === 'set-cookie')` fallback path
- `:427` write — `res.headers.delete('set-cookie')` (after hoisting into the Lambda result)
- `:531` write — `'set-cookie': cookies,` (API Gateway v1 multi-value output)
- `:613` write — `result.multiValueHeaders['set-cookie'] = cookies`
- `:615` write — `result.headers['set-cookie'] = cookies[0]` (ALB single-value output)
- `:659` write — `'set-cookie': cookies,` (Lattice/other result builder)

`adapters/aws-lambda/src/handler.ts` — same code, older line numbers (`src/adapter/aws-lambda` is kept only as a deprecated re-export; don't double-count)
- `:166` read, `:393` read (`has`), `:394`–`395` read (`getSetCookie`), `:397` read (`filter`), `:402` write (`delete`), `:500` write, `:579` write, `:581` write, `:622` write

## Gaps worth knowing

- `getSetCookie()` reads the header without naming it as a literal: `src/context.ts:422`, `src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts:419-420`, `adapters/aws-lambda/src/handler.ts:394-395`, plus tests at `src/context.test.ts:436,443,444,451,588`. These are reads of Set-Cookie that the literal rule can't see.
- `deleteCookie` (`src/helper/cookie/index.ts`) writes an expired Set-Cookie indirectly via `setCookie`, so it has no literal of its own.
- `getCookie` reads the request `Cookie` header, not `Set-Cookie`.
